description: E_inter edges for bipartite matchup graph. For each attacking canonical role idx, lists the 1-2 defending canonical role indices it directly opposes. Home team attacks, away team defends. Indices reference canonical_roles.json (0=GK,1=RB,2=RCB,3=CB,4=LCB,5=LB,6=CDM,7=CM,8=CAM,9=W,10=ST).

matchups.rationale: GK directly faces the opposition striker in long-ball / pressing situations. Also used to model GK distribution under press.
Attacking RB overlaps and faces the opposing left winger and, when the RB advances into the final third, the LCB stepping across to cover.
RCB in possession faces the opposition striker pressing and, in wide systems, a dropping wide forward.
Central CB directly opposes the central striker. In two-striker systems the same canonical slot covers both CBs.
Mirror of RCB: faces striker and right winger dropping to press.
Attacking LB overlapping faces the opposing right winger and, when advanced, the RCB covering across.
CDM in possession is pressed by the opposition CAM or central midfielder dropping to screen. Key axis in high-press vs double-pivot matchups.
CM drives into space and faces the opposing CDM or peer CM. Mid-block sides use the CM slot to screen central penetrations.
CAM / second striker operates between the lines and is picked up by the opposing CDM or a stepping CB in low-block shapes.
Wide forward (both wingers collapsed to one canonical slot) directly opposes the opposition fullbacks. In five-back systems this maps to wing-backs.
Centre forward directly opposes the central defenders. In three-back systems the middle CB (idx 3) is the primary matchup; RCB (idx 2) is secondary.

edge_list_note: Format: [attacking_canonical_idx, defending_canonical_idx]. In graph_builder.py, home attacking node i connects to away defending node (11 + defending_canonical_idx). The [7,7] entry is CM-vs-CM: both sides share the same canonical slot, so in the bipartite graph this is home node 7 -> away node 18 (11+7), which is valid since they are distinct nodes.
